subject: Ask: temporary pricing variance for PrivateConnect delay (Cardinal Health)
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodai.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodai.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodai.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodai.com>
Date: 2028-08-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Ask: temporary pricing variance for PrivateConnect delay (Cardinal Health)

Team —

Quick summary: Cardinal Health is in final procurement but they flagged that our PrivateConnect (customer-managed VPC peering / private networking) is not yet available in their target region/stack. Their go-live for the pilot SKU is 9/15; without PrivateConnect they will not move forward.

What they are asking (informally): a short, limited commercial accommodation while we ship the PrivateConnect bits — they want either a time-limited price reduction for the first 3 months or a one-time onboarding allowance to offset the network/security work on their side. Estimated "cost" range they expect is ~USD 45k–60k over three months for the usage profile.

Why this matters now: this is a $1.2M/yr ARR ACV motion with an expected multi-year expansion. Losing momentum here would push their launch past Q4 and likely bury the deal. From a product perspective, PrivateConnect is in the backlog with an engineering ETA currently targeted for late September (per RED-7881) — there is a realistic chance of a 2–4 week slippage.

Ask: can we approve a temporary pricing variance (one of the two options below) that the sales team can offer with exec sign-off? I know we want to avoid setting precedents, so I propose:
- Option A (preferred by customer): 40% off per-unit rate for the first 90 days, capped at $50k gross concession; OR
- Option B: One-time onboarding credit of $50k applied to first invoice + standard pricing thereafter.

I attached the customer pricing flow they sent and a brief impact math.

Next steps: if we get a green light on a path (A or B) I will: 1) draft the note to Procurement, 2) route for legal redline limits, and 3) update the HubSpot deal with the concession terms.

Thanks —
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Strategic Account Manager | Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwoodai.com | +1 (415) 555-0183

Attachments: cardinal_pricing_flow.pdf, privateconnect_roadmap_slide.png

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodai.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodai.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodai.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodai.com>
Date: 2028-08-15T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Ask: temporary pricing variance for PrivateConnect delay (Cardinal Health)

+1 to urgency here. Quick notes from my side:
- Commercially, option B (one-time credit) reduces carry-forward pricing precedent risk — it's discrete and time-boxed.
- If we do Option A (40% for 90d) we should strongly cap by $50k and add a clause that this applies only to launches where PrivateConnect is the gating item and customer signs a 12-month minimum usage commitment.
- We should also insist on a rollback: after 90 days, pricing reverts and we reserve the right to bill any overage at standard rates; customer must agree in writing.

I'll own the customer-facing wording + HubSpot amendment. Monica, can you confirm expected ARR retention lift if we keep them on track vs slip? Need that to justify concession to Finance.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Director, Strategic Sales | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwoodai.com

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodai.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodai.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodai.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodai.com>
Date: 2028-08-15T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Ask: temporary pricing variance for PrivateConnect delay (Cardinal Health)

Thanks — ran the numbers with GTM. If we lose the 9/15 pilot start we: 1) push the expansion timelines by at least one quarter on average, and 2) risk losing a path to an additional $400k–600k upside in next 12 months (they baked expansion into their roadmap contingent on pilot success).

Recommendation: Option B (one-time onboarding credit of $50k) + require Cardinal to sign a 12-month minimum consumption addendum at current list rates, with a clause that the credit is applied only if the pilot invoices are paid on time. That gives Finance comfort and keeps the fix narrowly scoped.

I'll prepare the amendment and coordinate on the addendum. Also: curious to Laura — can Product accelerate any small scoped deliverable (network handshake docs, a limited-control-plane patch) to reduce the timeline? Even a partial PrivateConnect (no cross-region) could unblock them.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwoodai.com

Attachment: signed_moa_stub.pdf (placeholder the customer asked us to pre-fill)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodai.com>
To: Tim O'Neill <tim.oneill@cardinalhealth.com>, procurement@cardinalhealth.com
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodai.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodai.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodai.com>
Date: 2028-08-15T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Proposal: one-time onboarding credit to keep launch on schedule

Tim —

Thanks again for the candid conversation this morning. Per our follow-up internally, we would like to offer a limited commercial path to keep your pilot on the 9/15 timeline while PrivateConnect reaches GA in your environment.

Proposal (for Procurement):
- One-time onboarding credit of USD 50,000 applied to the first invoice.
- Cardinal Health signs a 12-month minimum consumption addendum at standard list rates.
- Credit is contingent on on-time payment of pilot invoices and does not alter ongoing list rates after the credit is applied.
- This is a one-off accommodation tied specifically to the PrivateConnect delivery timeline and is not precedent for other accounts.

If Procurement is comfortable, please confirm and we will provide the amendment and legal language.

Best —
Aditya
Aditya Rao
Director, Strategic Sales | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwoodai.com

[Attachment: proposed_amendment_draft.docx (stub)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodai.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodai.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodai.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodai.com>
Date: 2028-08-16T09:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Ask: temporary pricing variance for PrivateConnect delay (Cardinal Health) — Approved with conditions

Thanks for the clear summary and the impact math. I approve Option B (one-time onboarding credit of $50k) with the following explicit conditions:
1) The credit is explicitly time-boxed to this deal and will be documented in HubSpot + the Sales amendment.
2) Legal to add a non-precedent clause and the 12-month minimum consumption commitment.
3) Finance to track as a commercial concession against DEAL-CH-2028-07 and record in the monthly commercial concessions report.
4) Product to commit to the current RED-7881 timeline; if the delivery slips more than 21 days beyond current ETA, we will re-evaluate any further accommodations.

Monica — please proceed to prepare the amendment language; Aditya/Hannah, loop Procurement on the doc and get a signed acceptance. I'll notify Finance and Legal of the concession record.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
VP, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwoodai.com
